channel.title: Genesis recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Genesis G80, G90, GV70, GV80 fuel line may leak
item.description: Fuel can leak where the fuel pipe connects to the fuel rail, the part that feeds gasoline to the engine. A loose or faulty connection can let gasoline escape in the engine bay, where it can reach hot parts. You might smell gas or see drips under the front of the car. A dealer will check the connection and tighten it, or replace the pipe if needed, at no cost.

item.title: Hyundai and Genesis front seat belt anchors may detach
item.description: On certain Hyundai Ioniq 6, Santa Fe, Santa Fe Hybrid and Genesis G90 vehicles, the anchor that holds the driver's or front passenger's seat belt to the car can come loose and detach. If that happens, the seat belt cannot hold the person in place during a crash, so it will not protect them the way it should. Dealers will inspect the anchors and either reinforce or replace them at no charge.

item.title: Genesis G80 and GV80 dashboard display can go blank
item.description: A software problem can make the instrument panel display, the screen in front of you that shows your speed and fuel level, go blank. Without it you cannot see how fast you are going or how much fuel is left. Genesis says to turn off the HD radio feature until the fix is done. The repair is a free software update, sent to the car over the air or loaded by a dealer.

item.title: Genesis G90 driver-assist radar causes sudden unexpected braking
item.description: The radar sensor in the front corner of the car, used by the Highway Drive Assist system, can mistakenly think another vehicle is there. When that happens the car can brake hard on its own even though nothing is in the way. Being slowed suddenly at highway speed can surprise you and the drivers behind you. Genesis says to leave Highway Drive Assist switched off until the repair is done; the fix replaces the front bumper beam.

item.title: Genesis GV60 windshield trim can detach onto the road
item.description: The strip of stainless-steel trim along the top edge of the windshield can come loose and fall off the car. The main danger here is not to you but to people behind you, because a piece of metal lying in the road can cause another driver to crash. Dealers will replace the windshield molding at no cost. Owner letters are expected to start going out October 30, 2025, but you can already look your car up.

item.title: Genesis G90 and GV60 dashboard display may go blank
item.description: A software problem in these Genesis G90 and GV60 models can make the main dashboard display stop working. That is the screen that shows your speed and your warning lights. If it goes blank, you cannot see how fast you are going or whether the car is trying to warn you about something. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet the federal safety rule for controls and displays.

item.title: Genesis G80, GV80 and GV70 driver display can fail
item.description: A software error can make the display right in front of the driver stop working. That is the screen showing your speed, along with the warning lights for things like the brakes, the engine and the airbags. If it goes blank, you cannot see how fast you are going or whether the car is trying to warn you about a problem. These vehicles do not meet federal rules for displays. Dealers inspect and update the software free.

item.title: Hyundai and Genesis EVs can lose power from charging unit
item.description: A unit that keeps the small 12-volt battery topped up can be damaged and stop working. When that battery runs down, the car can lose drive power and stop moving, which could leave you stranded or cause a crash. Dealers will check the unit and its fuse, replace them if needed, and update the software, all free. If your vehicle was already fixed under the earlier 2024 recall, it still needs this new repair.

item.title: Genesis GV60 and GV80 backup camera may shut off
item.description: Hyundai is recalling certain 2024-2025 Genesis GV60 and 2025 GV80 vehicles. When you shift into reverse, the backup camera picture may shut off instead of showing on the screen. Without that picture, you cannot see what is directly behind the vehicle while you are backing up. Dealers will update the camera software at no cost, and owner notification letters were mailed September 11, 2024.

item.title: Hyundai and Genesis performance models: fuel pump can fail
item.description: The pump that sends gasoline to the engine can fail. If that happens, the engine loses power and the vehicle may slow down or stall while you are driving, possibly in traffic or at highway speed. Dealers will update the engine computer software and, if an inspection shows it is needed, replace the fuel pump assembly. Both repairs are free. Hyundai began mailing owner letters September 9, 2024, with some earlier warning letters sent September 3, 2024.

item.title: Genesis GV70, GV80, G80, G90 fuel pump failure
item.description: The fuel pump is the part that sends gasoline from the tank to the engine. On these vehicles it can fail. If it does, the engine stops getting fuel and the vehicle loses power to drive — it can slow down or stop moving while you are out on the road. Your dealer will inspect the fuel pump and replace the assembly at no charge. This recall is an expansion of an earlier one, so some vehicles are being covered for the first time.

item.title: Genesis GV70 can slip out of Park and roll
item.description: Water can get into the wiring that controls the transmission on some 2024 Genesis GV70s. That can cause a short circuit and make the car slip out of Park into Neutral on its own, meaning it could roll away after you walk away from it. Hyundai tells owners to shut the engine off and set the emergency parking brake every time they park until the repair is done. A dealer will fix or replace the wiring.

item.title: Hyundai IONIQ and Genesis EVs may lose drive power
item.description: Your vehicle has a part called the Integrated Charging Control Unit, which keeps the small 12-volt battery charged while you drive. Hyundai found this unit can be damaged and stop charging that battery. If that happens, the car can lose power to the wheels while you are driving. A dealer will check the unit and its fuse, replace them if needed, and update the software. Hyundai later issued a newer fix, so even cars already repaired need to go back.

item.title: Genesis G70, G80 and G90 turbo oil leak fire risk
item.description: Cars with the 3.3-liter turbocharged V6 have a small pipe that feeds oil to the left turbocharger. That pipe can break down over time and leak. Oil dripping onto hot engine parts can catch fire under the hood. Dealers will replace the pipe free of charge. This recall replaces an earlier one (19V-538), so even if your car was repaired under that recall, it still needs the new repair.

item.title: Genesis sedans: water in starter can cause engine fire
item.description: Water can get into the starter solenoid — a small electrical part that helps start the engine. Water there can cause a short circuit, which can start a fire under the hood. It can happen while you are driving or while the car is parked with the engine off. Hyundai says park outside and away from buildings, garages and carports until the repair is done. Dealers add a relay kit in the engine's fuse box at no cost.

item.title: Hyundai IONIQ 5, IONIQ 6, Genesis GV60: driveshaft can break
item.description: The shaft that sends power to the rear wheels of these electric vehicles may not have been heat-treated correctly when it was made. A shaft made this way can break while the car is under load, and the car then loses drive power. Losing power in traffic, on a hill, or while merging onto a highway can lead to a crash. Hyundai mailed owner letters on March 29, 2024. A dealer will replace the rear inner driveshaft at no cost.

item.title: Genesis G80, GV70 and GV80 fuel pump may fail
item.description: The fuel pump on these Genesis models can fail. The pump is what sends gasoline from the tank to the engine, so if it stops working the vehicle can lose drive power and you may not be able to keep up with traffic or get out of the way. A Genesis dealer will replace the fuel pump for free. Hyundai mailed owner letters in November 2023, so parts and the repair are available now. Call the dealer even if you never got a letter.

item.title: Genesis GV60 front passenger seat belt may not fasten
item.description: On some 2023 GV60s, the front passenger seat belt has a faulty locking part inside the belt reel. Because of it, the belt may not pull out far enough to reach the buckle, or it may not latch at all. If the belt does not work properly, it cannot hold the passenger in place during a crash. Dealers will inspect the front passenger belt and replace it at no cost if it is affected.

item.title: Genesis GV60 rear driveshafts may break, losing power
item.description: On these all-wheel-drive electric SUVs, the rear driveshafts — the spinning shafts that send power from the motor to the rear wheels — can crack and break apart. If one fails, the vehicle can lose the power that drives it forward, which could leave you slowing down or stopped without warning, including in traffic. A dealer will replace both the left and right rear driveshafts with new parts.

item.title: Genesis G90 seat belt tighteners may burst in crash
item.description: Your seat belts have a small device that yanks the belt tight the instant a crash happens. On these 2023 Genesis G90s, that device can blow apart when it goes off. If it does, metal pieces can fly loose inside the car and hit the people sitting there. It affects the driver's belt, the front passenger's belt, and the rear belts. Dealers fix it by installing a cap that holds the parts in place.

item.title: Genesis seat belt part may explode during a crash
item.description: Front seat belts have a small device that tightens the belt the instant a crash happens. In these vehicles that device can burst apart when it goes off, throwing metal pieces into the cabin that could hit and injure the driver or front passenger. The dealer will fit a cap over the part to hold it together, free of charge. GV60 owners got a warning letter first and will get a second letter when their repair is ready. Cars fixed under the earlier 2021 recall need this repair too.

item.title: Hyundai Sonata and Genesis G70 trunk release may fail
item.description: These cars have a release inside the trunk so anyone shut in can get out. On the vehicles being recalled, the trunk latch can become damaged, and when it does, the trunk may no longer open from the inside. Someone inside the trunk could become trapped and injured. Nothing about how the car drives or stops is affected, but it is worth keeping children from playing in or near the trunk until the dealer inspects the latch and replaces part of it.

item.title: Hyundai and Genesis seat belt pretensioners can explode in crash
item.description: On some 2021 Hyundai Elantra, Elantra Hybrid, Venue, Genesis GV80 and 2022 Genesis GV70 vehicles, the front seat belts have a device that tightens the belt in a crash. That device can blow apart when it goes off, throwing metal pieces inside the car and hurting the people in the front seats. Hyundai has since replaced this recall with newer ones, so even cars already fixed need the new repair.

item.title: Genesis G80 and GV80 fuel line may leak gasoline
item.description: On these cars with the 2.5-liter turbo engine, the metal tube that carries gasoline from the pump to the engine may not seal tightly where it connects. Fuel can seep out of that joint. If the leaking gas reaches a spark or hot surface, it can catch fire. The dealer fix is a new high-pressure fuel tube, and it costs you nothing. Hyundai mailed letters to owners of affected Genesis vehicles in May 2021.

item.title: Genesis G80 anti-lock brake module can catch fire
item.description: These cars have a control box under the hood that runs the anti-lock brakes, the system that keeps the wheels from locking up when you stop hard. Inside that box, the electricity can take a wrong path and short out. If it does, the parts can get hot enough to start a fire in the engine compartment. This can happen while you are driving or while the car is parked and shut off. The dealer replaces a fuse on the unit.

item.title: Genesis G70 anti-lock brake module can catch fire
item.description: The G70 has a control box under the hood that runs the anti-lock brakes, the system that keeps the wheels from locking up during hard stops. The electricity inside that box can take a wrong path and short out. When that happens, it can get hot enough to start a fire in the engine compartment. It can happen while you are driving or while the car sits parked with the engine off. The dealer replaces a fuse on the unit.

item.title: Genesis G70 fuel pump defect can stall the engine
item.description: Some 2021 Genesis G70s with the 2.0-liter engine have a fuel pump with a tiny piece of leftover plastic inside. That bit can block the small nozzle that sends fuel to the engine. Without enough fuel, the engine can stall, meaning it suddenly stops running while you are driving. Hyundai dealers will inspect the fuel pump nozzle and repair it free of charge. Owner letters went out starting November 10, 2020.

item.title: Genesis G80 and G90 turbo oil leak fire risk
item.description: Certain 2018 Genesis G80 and 2017-2018 G90 sedans with the 3.3-liter turbocharged engine may have a loose seal on the pipe that carries oil to the turbocharger. Oil can seep out of that seal and drip onto the exhaust manifold, the very hot metal piece that carries exhaust gases away from the engine. Oil landing on metal that hot can catch fire. Hyundai dealers will replace the turbocharger oil supply pipe for you at no cost.

item.title: Genesis G80 passenger airbag sensor may misread empty seat
item.description: Your Genesis has a sensor system in the front passenger seat that decides whether the passenger airbag should turn on or off. On these cars, it can wrongly read the seat as holding an adult even when the seat is empty. If a child or infant is riding there, the airbag may fire in a crash instead of staying switched off. A dealer can reprogram the system, free of charge.

item.title: Genesis G80 and G90 windshield may come off
item.description: The front windshield and the rear window were glued in using the wrong primer, so the glue may not hold as strongly as it should. Over time that weaker bond can give way, and the windshield or rear window could come loose and detach while you are driving. Dealers will replace both the front and rear glass at no cost.
